observation_summary: FastDateFormat produces incorrect week-of-year values because it fails to use the provided locale when initializing the internal Calendar object used for formatting.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by an incorrect initialization of the GregorianCalendar object. The code was initializing the calendar using only the time zone, ignoring the locale. The fix involves passing the locale to the GregorianCalendar constructor, ensuring that locale-specific settings like firstDayOfWeek and minimalDaysInFirstWeek are correctly applied. This is a classic initialization error.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the change from 'new GregorianCalendar(mTimeZone)' to 'new GregorianCalendar(mTimeZone, mLocale)'
The bug report states: 'The issue looks to be that when creating the GregorianCalendar in format(Date), the locale is not passed.'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The procedural logic of formatting is correct; the issue is specifically that the underlying data structure (Calendar) was initialized with the wrong parameters.
While the locale is a parameter, the issue is not a mismatch in the interface contract, but rather the internal failure to use an available member variable during object initialization.
